item.title: Black travelers on Route 66 weren't welcome at most gas stations — except this one
item.description: Threatt Filling Station in Luther, Okla., was the first Black-owned gas station on Route 66. At a time when Black families needed the Green Book to find places to stay, eat, use the bathroom, it provided fuel and respite. (Image credit: Nick Oxford for NPR)

item.title: Bleeding, birth defects: Congo residents sue over alleged mining pollution
item.description: A landmark lawsuit in Congo sees 27 residents accuse a Chinese-owned copper and cobalt mine of poisoning their community and the government of failing to protect them. (Image credit: Marie Ruwet)

item.title: Meet Colombia's fuzzy 'water guardians'
item.description: páramos that supply much of the country's water.'/> High in the Colombian Andes, a growing number of volunteers are racing to save an unusual plant that helps supply water to millions — one tiny seedling at a time. (Image credit: John Otis for NPR)

item.title: Democrats probe whether Trump Jr.-aligned businesses benefit from government access
item.description: Investigators say companies with ties to Donald Trump Jr's investment firm, 1789 Capital, have profited since his father's reelection. (Image credit: Brandon Bell)

item.title: They attended Trump's meme coin dinner. It didn't go well
item.description: Trump's meme coin dinners have sparked intense controversy. These two guests attended his latest on Sunday — and agreed to provide NPR inside access. (Image credit: Courtesy of Morten Christensen and Gabriëlle Felen)

item.title: Doctors struggle to save babies after parents refuse vitamin K
item.description: Doctors are fighting an uphill battle against disinformation about routine vitamin K shots given to newborns in the hospital. It helps prevent a rare but devastating bleeding disorder. (Image credit: Kate Wells)

item.title: For workplace culture champions, Jensen Huang's return is 'unfathomable'
item.description: Some who have worked to promote diversity and inclusion in Silicon Valley say Jensen Huang's reinstatement as Nvidia's CEO sends a message that all that matters is money. (Image credit: Chung Sung-Jun)

item.title: Death of Nahel: French police officer who shot dead a teenage boy to stand trial for murder
item.description: A French police officer who shot and killed 17-year-old Nahel Merzouk during a traffic stop in June 2023 will stand trial for murder following a ruling by the Versailles appeals court. Merzouk's death at the hands of the police sparked intense riots in the sprawling suburbs surrounding Paris.

item.title: Russian drone flies into Poland during overnight strikes on Ukraine, Warsaw says
item.description: A Russian drone violated Polish airspace late on Monday night during Moscow's latest wave of long-range strikes on Ukraine, the Polish military said.

item.title: Heat deaths reached record high in England this year, data shows
item.description: Heat deaths reached a record high this year in England, new data shows.

item.title: Iran live updates: US land blockade of Iran 'impossible,' Araghchi says
item.description: President Donald Trump announced "major combat operations" against Iran on Feb. 28.

item.title: China to launch first space mission with a foreign astronaut
item.description: Pakistan's Muhammad Zeeshan Ali will become the first foreign astronaut to board China's Tiangong space station when the latest crew blasts off Wednesday. Ali said he would be carrying "the hopes of 250 million Pakistanis" with him.

item.title: ICG: "It's hard to imagine" Tripoli would risk its ties with Russia by approving a Ukrainian attack
item.description: Angela Diffley is pleased to welcome Claudia Gazzini, International Crisis Group's Senior Analyst for Libya. The Ukrainian attack on a Russian warship off the coast of eastern Libya has raised questions about Russian and Ukrainian military activity in the country. Gazzini discusses Russia's established military presence in eastern Libya and allegations that Ukrainian forces are operating in the west. She notes that while Russia is militarily present in eastern Libya, it also maintains "good commercial ties and political ties with western authorities as well." For Gazzini, the suggestion that Tripoli would approve such an operation "just sounds a bit too hazardous."

item.title: Jensen Huang’s return has calmed markets but fears of an AI bubble still run deep
item.description: Nvidia's decision to bring back Jensen Huang as CEO pushed the AI computing company's stocks up more than 30 percent Monday. But the model of circular financing increasingly underwriting the AI boom still has some analysts worried that the party can't last forever.

item.title: WATCH: Storms on both coasts threaten Thanksgiving week travel, Macy's parade
item.description: The storm set to slam New York City could ground Macy's parade balloons for the first time in 55 years.

item.title: WATCH: Amazon delivery drone crashes into Detroit home
item.description: Video shows workers removing an 80-pound Amazon delivery drone from a roof after it crashed into a home in suburban Detroit. Amazon said it's looking into the incident.

item.title: Collapse of COP31: 'This deal was a bad deal and better no deal than a bad deal'
item.description: François Picard is joined by Ireland's former environment minister Eamon Ryan following the collapse of COP31 in Antalya, Turkey. "Political science trumps climate science still," Ryan reacted. The talks failed after the European Union and up to 100 countries refused to accept a final text that abandoned earlier commitments to transition away from fossil fuels.

item.title: AFCON 2025: CAS set to hand down ruling on controversial final
item.description: The Court of Arbitration for Sport will deliver its ruling this Tuesday on the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations final. Senegal won the match on the pitch, but Morocco were awarded the trophy following an appeal to the CAF.

item.title: Live: Russian strikes on Ukraine’s Zaporizhzhia kill two people and wound dozens more
item.description: A Russian attack killed two people in the Ukrainian city of Zaporizhzhia overnight, regional governor Mykhailo Semikin said on Tuesday. Some 40 people, four of them children, were also wounded in the strikes, the governor added. Follow our liveblog for all the latest updates.

item.title: Trump owned at least $12 million in Nvidia stock at the end of last year
item.description: President Donald Trump owned at least $12 million in Nvidia stock at the end of 2025, according to his annual financial disclosure report reviewed by ABC News.

item.title: Nearly four million in destitution across UK, study suggests
item.description: The number of people in destitution across the UK is at a record level, according to new research, as approximately 3.8 million struggled to access basic necessities last year.

item.title: Jensen Huang's surprise return to Nvidia sparks mixed reactions in Washington
item.description: US President Donald Trump praised Nvidia's decision Monday to reinstate Jensen Huang as chief executive, as Democratic leaders vowed investigations and prominent Republicans questioned whether his return posed a national security risk.

item.title: Gisele Pelicot 'deeply shocked' as nude photos of her sent to media
item.description: Gisele Pelicot has said she is "deeply shocked" and "humiliated" after nude images of her were sent to the media without her consent to promote a new book about coercive control.

item.title: US flew surveillance drone over Mexico to help capture top drug lord
item.description: Mexican officials say the United States flew a surveillance drone over Mexican territory to help locate and capture one of the country's most wanted drug traffickers. The operation led to the arrest of Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, known as 'El Chapo Isidro'.

item.title: Sky News documentary wins International Emmy
item.description: Sky News has won an International Emmy for 24 Hours In The Kill Zone.

item.title: Illicit substances found in one in eight vapes seized from students
item.description: One in eight vapes seized in schools by the Metropolitan Police contained illicit drugs including spice and THC, a new operation has shown.

item.title: Victims failed at every step of criminal justice system - report
item.description: Victims of crime are being failed at every step of the criminal justice system, a major new report has warned.

item.title: Zelensky urges four-way peace talks with Russia, Europe and US 'as soon as possible'
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky is calling for a new round of negotiations involving Ukraine, Russia, the United States and European leaders, saying Kyiv is ready to meet as early as Tuesday.

item.title: Donald Trump given chance to erase his criminal record
item.description: Donald Trump has been offered a possible way to erase his criminal conviction for making hush money payments to adult film star Stormy Daniels.

item.title: 14 countries acknowledge ICJ ruling of genocide against Rohingya
item.description: Fourteen countries from Europe, Africa and Oceania have acknowledged a landmark ruling by the International Court of Justice (ICJ) that Myanmar committed genocide against its Rohingya minority, calling on the country to comply with its obligations under international law. The United Kingdom separately announced sanctions against five senior Myanmar military figures and said it would formally recognise the genocide.

item.title: NATO vows space defence after Russia nuclear satellite report
item.description: NATO chief Mark Rutte said Monday the alliance would defend against threats in space when asked about German media reports that Russia may be preparing to launch a nuclear-armed satellite. The media reports, citing unnamed German military and BND spy agency sources, said Moscow was thought to be planning such a launch in the coming weeks, giving it the capability to destroy other satellites. FRANCE 24's Laurent Berstecher reports.

item.title: California Democrat Rep. Gomez resigns following ethics report on sexual misconduct allegations
item.description: California Congressman Rep. Jimmy Gomez says he will resign after a House Ethics report concluded Gomez's actions violated House rules by "making unwelcome sexual advances." (Image credit: Heather Diehl)

item.title: What led to Democrats' sweeping victories in Georgia: ABC News analysis
item.description: ABC News analyzes factors of why Democrats performed well in Georgia on Election Night.

item.title: Africa disappointed with COP31 outcome
item.description: In tonight's edition: The COP31 climate summit in Turkey has failed to reach an agreement, exposing deep divisions over fossil fuels and climate finance. Also, DR Congo's Félix Tshisekedi and Kenya's William Ruto agree to restore relations and boost regional cooperation. And determined to help their children, parents in a South African township have transformed a discarded shipping container into a sensory room.

item.title: Jensen Huang reinstated as Nvidia CEO
item.description: In a stunning U-turn, Nvidia's board has reinstated Jensen Huang as the company's President and CEO. The announcement came just days after the board rejected a petition calling for the tech titan's return. US President Donald Trump said had personally got in touch with the board to advocate for his return. Nvidia's stock surged 32%, adding nearly $1 trillion to its market cap while the rest of Wall Street also rallied.

item.title: 'A war of unmanned machines, AI and total transparency of the battlefield'
item.description: Speaking with FRANCE 24's Sharon Gaffney, Nobel Peace Prize laureate Oleksandra Matviichuk, Director of the Centre for Civil Liberties, says that today's war in Ukraine "is a war of unmanned machines, AI, total transparency of the battlefield, mass drones attacks and long range weapons, and this means we have to rethink how to protect human beings".

item.title: LIVE: ABC News Live
item.description: 24/7 coverage of breaking news and live events

item.title: Libya's east seeks UN probe into claims Ukrainian military present in west
item.description: Authorities in divided Libya's east called on Monday for the United Nations to investigate claims that Ukrainian forces were present in the country's west, as they lodged a complaint over Ukrainian attacks on two Russian ships off Benghazi. The strikes on Sunday, claimed by Kyiv, come as Ukraine steps up strikes against Russia far from the front lines of their war. FRANCE 24's Emerald Maxwell reports.

item.title: Trump backs Nvidia boss's return but top Democrat vows probe
item.description: US President Donald Trump praised Nvidia's decision Monday to reinstate Jensen Huang as chief executive, as top Senate Democrat Chuck Schumer vowed to investigate potential wrongdoing amid mounting national security concerns. Trump also posted a doctored version of the famous photograph of him raising his fist after surviving a 2024 assassination attempt, replacing himself with Huang, who brandished a red bra beneath an Nvidia flag. FRANCE 24's Fraser Jackson reports from Washington.

item.title: How far will Ukraine war spread? Kyiv targets Russian vessels in Libya
item.description: Talk about a spillover effect. In the Libyan port of Benghazi, Ukraine is claiming responsibility for the sinkings first of a Russian warship and then a cargo vessel. That's on top of the sanctioned ship struck in the Baltic Sea that's since strayed into Finland's waters. Are these legitimate targets?

item.title: Ukraine claims it sank Russian warship off Libya
item.description: Ukraine on Monday claimed it was behind strikes on two Russian vessels off Libya, including one that sank a modern warship, in the latest spillover from Moscow's invasion. The attacks on Sunday near the Libyan port of Benghazi come at a time when Ukraine has stepped up its daring strikes against Russia far from the frontlines in retaliation for Moscow's deadly invasion. FRANCE 24's Gulliver Cragg reports from Kyiv.

item.title: Nvidia reinstates Huang as CEO after Trump intervention
item.description: Nvidia on Monday reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive in a stunning reversal that President Donald Trump said followed his own direct contacts with the company's board. Huang resigned two weeks ago over an affair with a woman whom US intelligence agencies suspect of spying for China, a departure that sent Wall Street tumbling and stoked fears for a US economy reliant on the AI investment boom. FRANCE 24's Carys Garland and Wassim Cornet report.

item.title: NYC Mayor Mamdani to undergo surgery this week following soccer injury
item.description: "I'm scared; it will be my first surgery," Mamdani said during an unrelated news conference on Monday.

item.title: 'Maintain control': UN chief calls for creation of global AI safety framework within a year
item.description: UN chief Antonio Guterres on Monday urged countries to agree on the creation of a global framework for managing the dangers posed by artificial intelligence within one year. Speaking at a summit in Barbados, he warned that taming the technology is vital if humanity is to stay in charge of its own future.

item.title: 'Deeply shocked': Gisèle Pelicot to sue publisher after nude photos used in book campaign
item.description: French feminist icon Gisèle Pelicot, who became a worldwide symbol against sexual violence during the 2024 rape trials against her husband and dozens of other men, said Monday she will take legal action after nude images of her were sent out without her permission to publicise a psychoanalyst's book on coercive control.

item.title: WATCH: Celebrating Tom Jackson's extraordinary life and legacy
item.description: The ESPN legend and former All-Pro linebacker died at 75.

item.title: Finland summons Russian ambassador after suspected airspace violation
item.description: Finland on Monday said it had summoned Russia's ambassador over a suspected violation of Finnish airspace by a Russian helicopter and after a Ukrainian drone strike on a Russian cargo ship located in the Gulf of Finland in recent days. Helsinki also condemned Moscow's escalating strikes on civilian targets in Ukraine.

item.title: WATCH: How AI tools can help lock in the lowest prices for holiday shopping
item.description: More than 40% of consumers have used AI assistants for online shopping, according to Adobe, and ABC News’ Becky Worley tried them to see how they can help with your shopping.

item.title: WATCH: NFL Sunday’s biggest moments
item.description: “GMA” has highlights from the San Francisco 49ers-Minnesota Vikings and Kansas City Chiefs-Arizona Cardinals games, plus a preview of Monday night's Cincinnati Bengals-Washington Commanders matchup.

item.title: FBI's national crime database targeted in hack, Trump says
item.description: President Donald Trump confirmed on Saturday that the FBI’s National Crime Information Center database was targeted in a hack.

item.title: Dems holding 12 debates in 2028 cycle, requiring candidates denounce 'dark money'
item.description: The Democratic National Committee announced on Monday that it will hold 12 primary debates in the 2028 presidential primary cycle.

item.title: Deadly fire at confectionery factory kills 24 as rescuers search for dozens still missing
item.description: A deadly fire that tore through a confectionery factory in Indonesia has claimed the lives of 24 people, with 34 others still missing.

item.title: Democrat Chuck Hubbard wins recount, flips North Carolina US House seat
item.description: Democratic Chuck Hubbard will win the election in North Carolina's 5th congressional district, the Associated Press projects.

item.title: Rahm Emanuel: Schumer should commit to stepping down as leader after next Congress
item.description: Former Chicago Mayor Rahm Emanuel, a potential 2028 presidential candidate, joined "This Week" to discuss what Democrats should do after their historic midterm victory.

item.title: DNI Clayton: Putin is 'not America's friend in Ukraine'
item.description: The director of national intelligence appeared on ABC's "This Week" Sunday.

item.title: Man who was lured to remote villa and held for 15 hours rescued after being tied up and beaten
item.description: A man has been rescued after he was lured to an isolated villa, held for 15 hours, tied to a chair, beaten, and threatened with death, police in Spain say.

item.title: Meet the Ukrainian energy workers dodging drones to bring people's electricity back
item.description: "The first thing the guys and I do is look at where we can hide."

item.title: At least 11 dead after suspected cartel leader 'El Chapo Isidro' captured in Mexico
item.description: An outburst of violence has killed at least 11 people after Mexican authorities captured suspected cartel leader Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, known as El Chapo Isidro.

item.title: WATCH: Tips for hosting Friendsgiving this year
item.description: Digital creator Kerra Masella shares her tips for planning and hosting a Friendsgiving celebration, from getting organized ahead of time to making friends feel welcome around the table.

item.description: Katy Nastro, travel correspondent at Flighty, shares what travelers can do to protect themselves.

item.description: Trump said the three countries made strides in advancing denuclearization talks.

item.title: WATCH: New health warning on doomscrolling: What to know and tips to break the habit
item.description: A Lancet Psychiatry report calls problematic internet use a global health concern, affecting more than 1 in 10 people. ABC News’ Dr. Jennifer Miao explains the impact and how to protect yourself.

item.title: WATCH: Reporter goes undercover as porch pirate
item.description: A New York Times reporter went undercover as a porch pirate to help identify the best ways to keep your home and packages safe as package deliveries ramp up this holiday season.

item.title: WATCH: Riverboat captain celebrates more than 50 years on the Mississippi River
item.description: ABC News' Danny New talks to riverboat captain Robbie Mitchell, who is marking a major milestone aboard the legendary steamboat Natchez.

item.title: WATCH: New video angle shows moment of Brooklyn apartment building's deadly collapse
item.description: Dash cam video from a bus passing by shows the terrifying moment a three-story Brooklyn apartment building buckled and crumbled to the ground, killing eight people and injuring multiple others.

item.title: WATCH: Grand Theft Auto VI is back and shattering records
item.description: The excitement around the release of GTA VI is causing gamers to “call out sick” to play and has lit up Miami in Vice City colors. ABC News’ Ashan Singh dives into what the hype is all about.

item.title: Nidal Hasan is set to be executed. The military's other death row cases are in limbo
item.description: There are three other former soldiers who are on the military’s death row.
